cells.tense: Right now you are holding several live truths at once without settling them into a single story.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Take a practice you share and pass it on the way you received it, changing the part that no longer fits. Say why you changed that part, and listen to what comes back.
cells.core: Where a false thing has just come down, you can hold the whole of it — who is hurting, what broke, what somebody has to say out loud — and you do not hurry it into calm. Two people contradict each other and you wait, hearing what each is carrying before you decide anything. That is not a middle between two positions. It is closer to tuning a string to the note the space is actually sounding. When a group has just fallen apart, it usually splits three ways before anyone can think. You sit inside all three at once. When you pass any of it on, do not hand over the inherited version as if it were settled. Teach it the way it came to you, change the one part that has stopped fitting, and say the change out loud. That is the difference between handing something down and letting it live in the hands that took it.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the whole of it without forcing one note.
cells.verb: Tune the instrument to the tone that is actually sounding
cells.place: In a space where something false has just come down

cells.tense: You are settling how the disagreement ends before anyone has finished saying it.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Find what you have been smoothing over early. Say the part you left out, to the person it touches, and leave the space unsettled afterward.
cells.core: You read a room's temperature sooner than most, and that is the gift. What it is doing now is reading that temperature before the people have finished speaking. Two of them are halfway into saying what they actually disagree about, and you are already arranging the agreement. The disagreement was the part that mattered. When you land the harmony first, the note that was about to break through gets covered over, and nobody hears it. Next time a group is about to separate, do not reach for the blend. Follow the part of you already pulling somewhere real — the feeling with something behind it — and take a step that way. Say the part you have been leaving out. It can land badly. That is allowed. The clearing you have been bracing for arrives once the true note has been played.

cells.tense: You were scattered by every voice last time, and you have been standing in its doorway since.
cells.act: let yourself be reached by what they are carrying
cells.ask: Stay with a person who is in something hard. Do not fix it, arrange it, or turn it into a lesson. Stay long enough that what they carry reaches you.
cells.core: A single hard thing can pull you in every direction at once, and lately that has been happening. Whose voice is loudest, whose face changed, what the silence meant — you have been tracking all of it, and the tracking is why there is no center to stand in. It is not that you cannot tune to what is there. It is that too many instruments have been playing at the same volume, and you have stopped hearing your own. Start smaller than that. One person, one hard thing, and you staying in it. Not fixing, not arranging, not making it mean something yet. Just let what they are carrying reach you while you keep your own side. That is how the tuning comes back — not by deciding to be centered, but by being reached by one real thing until the rest stops shouting.
cells.sheetLine: You are standing in a doorway that already closed.
cells.verb: Tune the instrument to the tone that is actually sounding

cells.tense: You are already moving with the new shape of that space, and you would call it following.
cells.act: hand one thing on in the way you were handed it
cells.ask: Choose a skill you have with others and show a single person how you were shown it. No edits, no improvements — the version you got. Then notice what they do with it.
cells.core: What broke in that space is still settling, and you are moving with the new shape of it — adjusting the parts, keeping the tone, doing the small work of letting it settle right. Asked how, you would say you were only following it. The adjustment is being made by your hand, and you have not said so. Nobody nearby has reason to think otherwise. What you have is a way of handing things on that you learned from someone, and it mostly works. Choose a skill you do well among the others, and show a single person the way you were shown it. No adjustments, no improvements — the version you were given. Notice what they make of it. That is where the tuning shows up in your hands, not just in the space around you.
